$TGT options flow lesson: volume and open interest answer different questions. Volume counts contracts traded during the session. Open interest is the standing balance from the prior settle. The two should not be treated as interchangeable. The alert snapshot shows $3.6M in the Dec 18 $155 puts. Volume was 21.1x standing open interest at capture. Intraday volume does not establish whether a position was opened or held; the next settled open interest is the check.

$TGT 
 
HSBC upgraded Target to Buy from Hold today and raised its target to 190 from 125. That is a 52 percent raise, sitting well above the Street average near 166. 
 
Analyst Joe Thomas also lifted his fiscal 2027 earnings estimate to 10.61 from 8.26, up 28 percent. His case: better sales create operating leverage, pushing margins toward 6 percent. 
 
The read behind it: second-quarter growth was traffic-driven. Shoppers visited more often instead of spending more per trip. Thomas says that shows Target is rebuilding traffic without cannibalizing its store base. 
 
The wrinkle: Target cut prices on nearly 2,000 items Tuesday, on top of 10,000-plus over the past year. Traffic built on price cuts is real until the margin math shows up. 
 
Shares around 157 today, up 63 percent on the year.

Walmart  The retailer is positioned through a combination of partnerships with external AI platforms and investments in its own capabilities. Its scale, logistics network, pricing power and broad product selection remain important regardless of where the shopping journey begins. UBS said the key challenge may be protecting Walmart’s high-margin advertising business and broader ecosystem economics rather than simply maintaining sales growth. 
Target   The retailer retains competitive advantages from its scale and logistics capabilities. $TGT Target lowers prices on nearly 2,000 home, apparel products 
 
Target Corporation is lowering prices on nearly 2,000 home and apparel & accessories items, helping busy families find even more affordable options as holiday shopping gets underway. The latest reductions build on the more than 10,000 prices Target has lowered over the past year, continuing to make it easier for families to afford the things that matter to them. Guests will see price reductions across nearly 2,000 on-trend items and refreshed staples, including: Apparel and shoes: Lower prices across women's, men's, infant and toddler apparel and shoes for the entire family, with select items priced 20% or more lower than last year.  
 
Examples include: Women's long-sleeve tees are now $12, down from $15; The average price of women's shoes is $35, down from $40 last year - with nearly 70% of new items priced below last year's styles; The average price of kids' rain and winter boots is down approximately 15% from last year. Home: A fully refreshed bedding assortment, with prices 15% lower, on average, including: Threshold queen comforters are now $69, down from $89; Room Essentials queen comforters are now $40, down from $50; Threshold performance queen sheets are now $50, down from $55.
